title: Fabric Visor: orthogonal route+model inspector for latency, throughput and token-cost lanes
creator: Ava Chen
description: High-level: Design a compact, orthogonal inspector panel (Fabric Visor) that surfaces per-route and per-model performance signals in a single horizontal canvas. The panel combines three coordinated lanes: (1) adaptive latency ribbons (P50/P90/P99 quantiles), (2) throughput stream (requests/sec and concurrency bands), and (3) token-cost lanes (token counts, prefix cache hit rates, and estimated $/k-token). The goal is a single glance surface for SREs and platform engineers to triage regressions, spot cost anomalies, and drive rollout decisions. This ticket covers UI spec, prototype flows, accessibility checks, and review synthesis with PM/Engineering for implementation handoff.
acceptance_criteria: A responsive Fabric Visor UI prototype exists in Figma with desktop + compact (sidecar) variants
Latency ribbons show P50/P90/P99 and allow toggling to view absolute vs. relative delta to baseline
Throughput stream renders steady-state concurrency bands and highlights capacity spikes with annotations
Token-cost lane computes estimated cost overlay per-request and supports toggling cache-hit-adjusted view
Rollout snapshot strip with canary toggle and quick rollback affordance is included and annotated for dev handoff
Design tokens and spacing variables are documented for implementation (CSS vars / tokens list)
Prototype contains example anomaly drill flow linking to timeline and suggested runbook actions
Design review feedback from PM and at least two engineers addressed and captured in comments
design_notes: We intentionally separate the three lanes visually (soft-contrast separators) so engineers can scan orthogonally: ribbons (vertical jitter) on top, throughput stream in the middle with a condensed sparkline stack, and token-cost at the bottom with stacked area for cache-adjusted vs raw tokens. Use a muted palette for baseline, saturated for anomalies. Rationale: previous dashboards overloaded a single chart; orthogonal lanes keep correlation visible without overlay clutter. Accessibility: ensure color contrast for P99 and anomaly highlights and provide non-color encodings (patterned fills and aria-live values).
decisions: Use quantile ribbons rather than multiple line overlays to reduce perceptual clutter
Expose a lightweight canary toggle in the header (on/off) with inline latency delta so operators can make quick rollback calls
Cost estimates are derived client-side from token counts + model rate table; show confidence tier and link to cost profile in Console
Prototype will include an interactive anomaly drill linking to the trace/metrics view rather than trying to show raw traces inside the visor
